tools.name: create_app
tools.description: Create a new application from a natural language prompt. The AI generates a complete web app with pages, components, styling, and data models. Returns a job_id - poll get_job_status to track progress. When the job is done, the app is ready.

tools.name: agency_create_client
tools.description: Agency mode only. Create or update a client record for an account-level agent. This does not create a verified Fine Structure user account and does not transfer ownership.

tools.name: agency_list_clients
tools.description: Agency mode only. List client records and app handoff status for the authenticated agent.

tools.name: agency_create_client_app
tools.description: Agency mode only. Create a new app owned by the agent, start generation, and create a claim link for the client. Ownership transfers only when the invited client logs in with the same email and accepts the claim link.

tools.name: agency_create_claim_link
tools.description: Agency mode only. Create a client claim link for an existing app owned by the agent. The client must log in with the invited email before ownership transfers.

tools.name: agency_get_claim_status
tools.description: Agency mode only. Inspect one handoff status without exposing the raw claim token.

tools.name: update_app
tools.description: Update an existing application with a new prompt. The AI modifies the app based on your instructions. Creates a Saved Version before the update. Returns a job_id - poll get_job_status to track progress.

tools.name: publish_app
tools.description: Publish an app - freeze current state and make it live at a URL. Also configures whether the public URL is open, app-login gated, private, or inferred from the app.

tools.name: get_platform_guide
tools.description: Return a machine-readable Fine Structure / FSe2 guide for AI agents. Call this at the start of an MCP session to learn app files, entities, safe edit workflows, validation, publishing, A/B testing, secrets, and platform rules.

tools.name: get_recommended_workflow
tools.description: Return the recommended MCP tool sequence for a task type. Use this before creating apps, editing files, seeding data, publishing, setting up A/B tests, restoring versions, or configuring secrets/integrations.

tools.name: get_job_status
tools.description: Poll the status of an async generation job. Use this after create_app or update_app to know when the job is done. Returns status ('running' or 'done'), progress events, and result summary when complete.

tools.name: get_app_status
tools.description: Get app overview: files, published state, URL, active jobs.

tools.name: get_app_links
tools.description: Return editor, preview, published path, subdomain, and custom-domain links plus whether each works for anonymous visitors, app users, or Studio users based on publish and auth settings.

tools.name: list_app_domains
tools.description: List an app's platform path, subdomain, and configured custom domain with verification, SSL, primary-domain, redirect, publish, and login-gating status.

tools.name: set_app_subdomain
tools.description: Set or clear the app platform subdomain - the '<subdomain>.<base domain>' host Fine Structure already serves the app on. Runs the same ownership, format, reserved-name and uniqueness checks as the Studio subdomain field because it calls the same model function. Replacing a subdomain takes effect imm

tools.name: check_subdomain_available
tools.description: Check whether a platform subdomain can be claimed before calling set_app_subdomain. Returns available plus a status of available, invalid, reserved, taken, current, or empty, with the exact reason. Pass app_id (an app you own) to have that app's own current subdomain reported as 'current' instead of

tools.name: add_custom_domain
tools.description: Attach or replace the app custom domain through the same Fine Structure Studio custom-domain flow. Returns exact DNS verification and routing records for the user to configure at their DNS provider.

tools.name: get_domain_verification
tools.description: Return the exact DNS records and instructions required to verify and route the app custom domain.

tools.name: check_domain_verification
tools.description: Check Fine Structure custom-domain verification and SSL status for the configured custom domain, then save the latest status.

tools.name: set_primary_domain
tools.description: Set which app host should be treated as primary for generated links and custom-domain redirects.

tools.name: remove_custom_domain
tools.description: Remove the configured custom domain from the app and clean up the platform-side hostname registration when possible.

tools.name: get_domain_ssl_status
tools.description: Return SSL/certificate status and pending certificate validation DNS records for the app custom domain.

tools.name: configure_domain_redirects
tools.description: Configure custom-domain redirect policy: primary domain, optional www/root redirect, and HTTPS enforcement.

tools.name: list_apps
tools.description: List owned and accepted Studio-shared applications, newest activity first. Returns up to `limit` apps per call plus the total count; page with `offset` when the account has more. Accepted editors can edit shared source; viewers can read it. Publishing, records, domains and security administration re

tools.name: get_app_files
tools.description: Get the file tree for an app with paths and byte sizes.

tools.name: read_app_file
tools.description: Read one source file from an app's virtual filesystem. Paths follow the Fine Structure app file API, documented at https://finestructure.ai/api/mcp/docs.

tools.name: read_app_files
tools.description: Read several source files from an app's virtual filesystem. Paths follow the Fine Structure app file API, documented at https://finestructure.ai/api/mcp/docs.

tools.name: write_app_file
tools.description: Create or replace one file in an app's virtual filesystem. Creates a Saved Version before changing content. Paths and file model follow the Fine Structure app file API, documented at https://finestructure.ai/api/mcp/docs.

tools.name: patch_app_file
tools.description: Patch one file by replacing exact text. Safer than full overwrite for targeted edits. Creates a Saved Version before changing content. Paths follow the Fine Structure app file API, documented at https://finestructure.ai/api/mcp/docs.

tools.name: rename_app_file
tools.description: Rename or move one app source file atomically. Internally stages an upsert at new_path and a delete at old_path, validates the resulting app state, and creates a Saved Version before applying.

tools.name: get_app_detail
tools.description: Deep introspection of an app: entities, pages, settings, integrations, environment variables, and file structure. Use this to understand what an app contains before updating it.

tools.name: get_entities
tools.description: Get all entity (data model) schemas for an app, with record counts. Each entity has fields, types, and relationships.

tools.name: query_entity
tools.description: Query app data records for one entity with optional exact-match filters.

tools.name: seed_entity
tools.description: Compatibility tool for starter-record creation. Inserts directly for the authenticated app owner; by default it only seeds an empty entity (skip_if_not_empty).

tools.name: create_entity_records
tools.description: Create/insert records in one app entity. Executes directly for the authenticated app owner and returns the created record ids.

tools.name: update_entity_record
tools.description: Compatibility tool that updates one record by ID. Executes directly for the authenticated app owner.

tools.name: update_entity_records
tools.description: Update exact records. Select explicit record_ids or exact-match filters and provide shared changes, or provide per-record updates. Executes directly for the authenticated app owner; expected_count aborts the write on a mismatch.

tools.name: delete_entity_records
tools.description: Delete exact records by ID or exact-match filters. Executes directly for the authenticated app owner; pass expected_count as a safety check to abort on a mismatch.

tools.name: get_pages
tools.description: Get all pages in an app with their file paths and sizes.

tools.name: get_errors
tools.description: Get recent runtime errors for an app (last 20). Useful for diagnosing issues before updating.

tools.name: get_app_analytics
tools.description: Traffic analytics for an app's published site over a chosen window: total views, unique visitors, daily series, top pages, top referrer domains and device split.

tools.name: get_preview_url
tools.description: Return editor preview and published/public URLs for an app.

tools.name: list_saved_versions
tools.description: List restorable Saved Versions for an app, including versions created by MCP writes.

tools.name: create_change_set
tools.description: Create a staged file change set. Add multiple file changes, validate them as one app state, then apply atomically.

tools.name: add_file_change
tools.description: Stage one file upsert or delete inside a change set. Does not modify the live app until apply_change_set. Paths follow the Fine Structure app file API, documented at https://finestructure.ai/api/mcp/docs.

tools.name: validate_change_set
tools.description: Validate current app files plus staged change set files before applying.

tools.name: apply_change_set
tools.description: Apply a staged change set to the app. Creates a Saved Version before applying. Blocks on validation errors unless force=true.

tools.name: discard_change_set
tools.description: Discard a pending staged change set without changing app files.

tools.name: validate_app
tools.description: Run deterministic app checks: syntax, imports, routes/pages, entity schemas, missing entities, and recorded runtime errors.

tools.name: inspect_preview
tools.description: Return server-side preview context: URLs, persisted runtime/network errors, static clickable candidates, pages, and explicit live-browser availability.

tools.name: get_app_security_context
tools.description: Return safe security context for one owned app: owner id/email, Studio collaborators, generated-app members, route policies, entity policies, function policies, and recent security audit entries. Does not return secrets and does not grant access to other apps.

tools.name: set_route_policy
tools.description: Create or update a server-owned route policy for a generated app route.

tools.name: set_function_policy
tools.description: Create or update the server-owned access policy of a backend function (functions/<name>.js). Without a policy a function answers only to the app owner's Studio token (401 for app visitors and webhooks). Recipes: anonymous checkout step or inbound webhook/IPN -> require_auth=false; signed-in members

tools.name: invoke_function
tools.description: Run a backend function of an owned app exactly like the HTTP route and return its status and JSON. caller='owner' runs as the app owner; caller='anonymous' first evaluates the function policy as a public visitor and returns the 401/403 decision without running when access would be denied. Use it to

tools.name: create_platform_request
tools.description: Open a request to the Fine Structure platform team: a bug, a feature request or a question about the platform itself (not about the user's app). Use it when something in the platform blocks you instead of working around it. Give a reproduction the team can run (invoke_function / curl / the exact too

tools.name: get_platform_request
tools.description: One platform request with its full history: team replies, status changes (open | triaged | in_progress | needs_info | deployed | wont_fix) and what was deployed (commit, time). Pass since=<ISO timestamp> to get only the events after it.

tools.name: list_platform_requests
tools.description: Your account's platform requests, newest activity first. Call it at the start of a session with since=<the updated_date you last saw> to learn what changed: replies, needs_info questions to answer, deployments with their commit. Filters: app_id, status.

tools.name: reply_platform_request
tools.description: Add a reply or a finding to one of your platform requests without opening a new one, e.g. to answer a needs_info question (that reopens it).

tools.name: update_platform_request
tools.description: Platform team only: set the status of a request (open | triaged | in_progress | needs_info | deployed | wont_fix), attach the deployed commit and/or reply. deployed and needs_info mail the requester.

tools.name: set_entity_policy
tools.description: Replace server-side entity access policy. Optional action rules override read/write roles and can allow public create without public read, update, or delete. Omitting rules replaces any existing action rules with read/write role behavior.

tools.name: list_app_members
tools.description: List generated-app runtime users/members for an app. This is separate from Studio project collaborators.

tools.name: invite_app_member
tools.description: Provision a generated-app runtime member with a role. This does not create a Studio collaborator, and the owner role cannot be assigned. password is required: ask the account owner which password the member should get. This tool never generates one, because a generated password would come back in th

tools.name: update_app_member_role
tools.description: Update a generated-app runtime member role. This cannot assign owner and cannot change the Fine Structure account owner.

tools.name: remove_app_member
tools.description: Remove a person's access to the app. They are blocked, as with block_app_member: their sessions end and the address can neither sign in nor sign up again. Nothing is deleted, and unblock_app_member gives the access back.

tools.name: get_app_security_audit
tools.description: Read recent server-side security audit events for an app.

tools.name: compare_saved_versions
tools.description: Compare two Saved Versions and return per-file additions, removals, modifications, and compact diffs.

tools.name: compare_current_to_version
tools.description: Compare the current app files to a Saved Version and return compact per-file diffs.

tools.name: restore_file_from_version
tools.description: Restore one file from a Saved Version instead of restoring the entire app. Creates a Saved Version before changing the file. Paths follow the Fine Structure app file API, documented at https://finestructure.ai/api/mcp/docs.

tools.name: create_entity_schema
tools.description: Create an entity schema file in entities/<Entity>.json. Creates a Saved Version before writing.

tools.name: update_entity_schema
tools.description: Replace or shallow-merge an existing entity schema file. Creates a Saved Version before writing.

tools.name: validate_entity_relationships
tools.description: Validate entity relationship metadata and *_id references against existing entity schemas.

tools.name: update_entity_metadata
tools.description: Set relationship/index metadata on an entity schema. This stores metadata in the schema file; DB index creation is automatic where supported by the platform.

tools.name: list_secret_keys
tools.description: List secret key names for an app. Secret values are never returned.

tools.name: set_secret
tools.description: Create or update one encrypted app secret. The secret value is never returned.

tools.name: delete_secret
tools.description: Delete one app secret by key.

tools.name: list_integrations
tools.description: List supported integrations and safe connected integration metadata for an app. Tokens/secrets are never returned.

tools.name: configure_integration
tools.description: Store safe non-secret integration metadata for an app. Use set_secret for API keys/tokens.

tools.name: list_ab_tests
tools.description: List the platform A/B tests configured for an app.

tools.name: create_ab_test
tools.description: Create a native Fine Structure A/B test between existing app pages. Use update_app first if a variant page still needs to be generated. Creates a Saved Version before the change.

tools.name: update_ab_test
tools.description: Update a native A/B test, including active state, variants, traffic, and conversion goal. Creates a Saved Version before the change.

tools.name: delete_ab_test
tools.description: Delete a native A/B test from an app. Creates a Saved Version before the change.

tools.name: get_ab_test_stats
tools.description: Get views, unique visitors, conversions, and conversion rates for an A/B test.

tools.name: get_app_metadata
tools.description: Read the saved public HTML-shell identity: name, description, language and image URLs/dimensions. Same settings as Studio SEO/GEO.

tools.name: set_app_metadata
tools.description: Update public HTML-shell metadata immediately, without AI, code edits, publishing or Saved Versions. Upload social_image/icon as base64 PNG/JPEG/WebP (max 5 MB, 4096px); null clears an image. Language sets HTML lang/dir and OG locale. For per-page cards, write optional seo.json and publish it; dynam

tools.name: preview_saved_version
tools.description: Prepare an isolated read-only Saved Version preview, if enabled by the deployment. Returns compiled files for an offline sandbox, never restores files or reads live records. Never execute the returned program with host credentials. Requires app access and versions:read.

tools.name: set_agent_owner_relay
tools.description: Set the owner's consent for one owned agent to relay reports from another owned agent (or all sources with '*'). Uses the same preference as the agent screen. Does not send a message or grant access to customer conversations.

tools.name: create_agent
tools.description: Create an autonomous AI agent on the user's Fine Structure account: a standing worker, not a chat session. It gets the platform's default safe tool policy and its own email address, it can read and write the app database, and once the owner phone is verified (see get_agent_whatsapp) it can message i

tools.name: list_agents
tools.description: List the AI agents on the user's account with id, name, role, status and FineMail address.

tools.name: schedule_agent_task
tools.description: Create a scheduled task for one of the user's agents. Supported schedule types: once (run_at ISO local time + timezone), interval (interval_minutes 5-1440), hourly, daily (time HH:MM + timezone), weekly (time + timezone + days_of_week 0=Sunday..6), cron (5-field expression + timezone), manual (only

tools.name: list_agent_tasks
tools.description: List scheduled tasks for one agent (or the whole account), including schedule, status and next_run_at.

tools.name: get_agent_whatsapp
tools.description: Read the WhatsApp state of the connected account: whether the owner's phone is verified, which platform numbers they can connect, and which conversations already route to which agent. Call this first whenever the user asks to talk to an agent on WhatsApp, and repeat its next_step to them.

tools.name: start_owner_phone_verification
tools.description: Send a 6-digit code over WhatsApp to the ACCOUNT OWNER's own phone. This is the one-time ownership proof required before a platform number can be connected, and it also unlocks agents messaging the owner. Ask the user for their own WhatsApp number first and send only to that. No WhatsApp Business ac

tools.name: confirm_owner_phone_verification
tools.description: Confirm the 6-digit code the owner received on WhatsApp from start_owner_phone_verification. On success the owner is verified: agents can message them, and platform numbers become connectable.

tools.name: attach_agent_whatsapp
tools.description: Connect a platform WhatsApp number to one of the account's agents, so the owner can message that number and reach that agent. Requires the owner to be verified first. Take phone_number_id from get_agent_whatsapp. A number already used by another account is still valid to connect: it answers only thi

tools.name: detach_agent_whatsapp
tools.description: Disconnect the owner's WhatsApp route from a platform number. Removes only this account's route; other accounts sharing the number keep theirs.

tools.name: list_agent_conversations
tools.description: List recent visible conversations belonging to one of your agents. Use get_agent_conversation to read replies and results.

tools.name: send_agent_message
tools.description: Talk to an existing agent or assign it work using its normal tools, memory, permissions and team. Omit conversation_id to start a new owner conversation; supply it to continue one. Returns acceptance and a durable task_id immediately, NOT a completed answer. Poll get_agent_task and read get_agent_co

tools.name: get_agent_conversation
tools.description: Read visible messages, answers and result links in an owned agent's conversation. Returns the newest page in chronological order. For older history, pass next_before_id as before_id. For new replies, omit before_id.

tools.name: get_agent_task
tools.description: Check a durable task returned by send_agent_message or list_agent_tasks. Includes the latest execution status and pending approvals, including before a run starts. Task scheduling state is separate from run outcome. Read the conversation for the actual answer; accepted/queued is not completed. Appro

tools.name: get_agent
tools.description: Read one agent: name, role, description, persona (its standing instructions), status, email address, WhatsApp number and which capability groups are switched on.

tools.name: update_agent
tools.description: Edit an agent's name, role, description or persona (its standing instructions). Only the fields given change; the previous text is replaced. Capabilities, channels and approvals stay as they are and are changed in Fine Structure.

tools.name: set_agent_status
tools.description: Pause, resume or archive an agent. paused: it stops working and keeps its setup. archived: it is retired from the account; use this when the owner asks to delete an agent. active: it works again. Tasks that came due while it was paused or archived were paused themselves and stay paused: the result l

tools.name: list_agent_activity
tools.description: What the account's agents did, newest first: each run with its agent, status, the tools it called, agent credits used and any error. Read the run's conversation with get_agent_conversation for the full answer.

tools.name: list_agent_approvals
tools.description: Actions the agents are holding until the owner approves them, such as a message to a customer or a payment. Each comes with a plain description and a review link. The owner approves or rejects them in Fine Structure.

tools.name: get_credit_balance
tools.description: The account's plan and both balances: build credits, which pay for creating and editing apps, and agent credits, which pay for agent runs.

tools.name: update_agent_task
tools.description: Change a scheduled task: title, instructions, schedule (same shape as schedule_agent_task), max_runs, or status active/paused. Only the fields given change. Returns the next run in UTC and in the schedule's timezone.

tools.name: archive_agent_task
tools.description: Remove a scheduled task from the agent's schedule. It never runs again and stays readable in the history. Use this when the owner asks to delete or cancel a task.

tools.name: run_agent_task_now
tools.description: Start one run of a scheduled task now, outside its schedule. The run does what the task's instructions say under the agent's permissions, so it can message people and it uses agent credits. Waits up to 15 seconds: it returns the finished task, or running true while the run goes on. Follow it with ge

tools.name: stop_agent_task
tools.description: Stop a task now: pause its schedule and cancel the run in progress, which stops at its next safe point. Safe to repeat. Resume it later with update_agent_task status active.

tools.name: cancel_agent_run
tools.description: Cancel one run in progress, for example a reply the agent is still working on. Work it handed to other agents is cancelled with it. Take run_id from list_agent_activity or get_agent_task.

tools.name: list_agent_goals
tools.description: An agent's goals: objective, success criteria, plan, status, progress, current step and the background runner task that works on it.

tools.name: create_agent_goal
tools.description: Give an agent a goal to pursue on its own. It works on it every interval_minutes, at most max_iterations times, under its own permissions, so a step can message people the agent is allowed to reach. Each step uses agent credits.

tools.name: update_agent_goal
tools.description: Change a goal's title, objective, success criteria, plan, iteration cap or status. paused stops its runner, active starts it again, completed and archived end it. Only the fields given change.

tools.name: archive_agent_goal
tools.description: Retire a goal: its runner stops and never runs again, and the goal stays readable. Use this when the owner asks to delete a goal.

tools.name: run_agent_goal_now
tools.description: Work one step of a goal now, outside its interval, under the agent's permissions; it can message people and uses agent credits. Waits up to 15 seconds, then returns running true while the step goes on.

tools.name: list_org_goals
tools.description: The owner's company-wide goals, the shared objectives every agent aligns to, with progress.

tools.name: create_org_goal
tools.description: Add a company-wide goal for the whole agent team to align to.

tools.name: update_org_goal
tools.description: Change a company-wide goal's title, objective, status (active, paused, done, cancelled) or progress (0-100). Only the fields given change.

tools.name: list_org_goal_updates
tools.description: The progress notes agents wrote on a company-wide goal, newest first.

tools.name: list_agent_triggers
tools.description: What starts an agent on its own: event, schedule, watch and webhook triggers, with their instructions, status and last fire. A webhook's URL carries its secret and is shown only on the agent's screen.

tools.name: create_agent_trigger
tools.description: Add a trigger that starts the agent with these instructions: event (event_type such as lead.created, with an optional source), schedule (a schedule object) or watch. Each start is a run under the agent's permissions and uses agent credits. Its approval rules stay as set in Fine Structure, and a webh

tools.name: update_agent_trigger
tools.description: Change a trigger's name, type, event, source, instructions, schedule or status (active or paused). Only the fields given change. Archive it with archive_agent_trigger.

tools.name: archive_agent_trigger
tools.description: Retire a trigger: it never starts the agent again and stays readable. Use this when the owner asks to delete a trigger.

tools.name: run_agent_trigger_now
tools.description: Fire a trigger once now as a test: the agent runs its instructions under its permissions, so it can message people and uses agent credits. Returns at once with the task that runs it; follow it with get_agent_task.

tools.name: list_agent_memories
tools.description: What an agent has learned and kept: long-term facts and insights, newest first, optionally only those about one customer.

tools.name: list_team_templates
tools.description: Ready-made agent teams (for example a sales or a support company) that create_agent_team builds in one step, with each member's role.

tools.name: create_agent_team
tools.description: Create a whole team of agents from a template, wired to work together, optionally adapted to the owner's requirements and company name. The new agents start active with the platform's default safe permissions and can message only their verified owner until channels are connected in Fine Structure.

tools.name: list_agent_templates
tools.description: Ready-made single agent templates: role, description and suggested persona, for create_agent.

tools.name: list_connections
tools.description: The account's connected accounts and services (each mailbox, Drive view, MCP server, app account and so on is one connection), and whether Google Drive, Facebook and a mailbox are connected. Connecting, disconnecting and sharing a connection with an agent are done on the Connections screen in Fine S

tools.name: list_connection_catalog
tools.description: Every service the platform can connect, with whether this account has connected it, whether one-click sign-in is available, and its connections.

tools.name: get_connection_access
tools.description: Which of the owner's agents and apps may use one connection (from list_connections).

tools.name: get_connection_status
tools.description: Status of the account-level connections: Facebook, Google Drive, TikTok and the social accounts connected through Zernio (Instagram, LinkedIn and others), including any that need to be reconnected. refresh true asks Zernio for the live state.

tools.name: list_facebook_ad_accounts
tools.description: The ad accounts the connected Facebook account reaches, and which of them agents may use (an empty allowed list means all).

tools.name: search_connectable_apps
tools.description: Third-party apps an agent can be connected to (thousands, through the apps lane), with the account's own connections. Search by name.

tools.name: list_connectable_app_tools
tools.description: What an agent could do with one third-party app once it is connected: its actions.

tools.name: get_make_migration_report
tools.description: Read every scenario in the owner's connected Make account and grade what moves to Fine Structure fully, partly or by hand. Read-only.

tools.name: list_event_connections
tools.description: Incoming-events sources: external systems that send events to the account (a form, a shop, a payment provider), each with its status (draft, active, paused) and its mapping steps.

tools.name: list_event_connection_events
tools.description: The latest 100 events a source received and what each did: status, step results, errors.

tools.name: list_event_connection_revisions
tools.description: The saved versions of a source's configuration.

tools.name: preview_event_connection
tools.description: Dry run: show what a source would do with a sample event (its identity, which steps match, the mapped contact fields). Nothing is written or sent.

tools.name: pause_event_connection
tools.description: Pause an incoming-events source: events that arrive are kept and wait, and none is processed until the owner activates it again on the Connections screen.

tools.name: list_knowledge_notebooks
tools.description: The knowledge notebooks of the owner's Business Brain, or of one app: title, folder, how many documents and their state. Agents and apps answer from notebooks they are given.

tools.name: list_knowledge_folders
tools.description: The folders the notebooks are filed in, nested.

tools.name: list_knowledge_documents
tools.description: The documents (sources) of a notebook: name, type, status (queued, processing, ready, failed), size and error.

tools.name: get_knowledge_notebook_overview
tools.description: A notebook's overview: the summary written from its sources, document counts by state, and which sources are ready.

tools.name: read_knowledge_document
tools.description: The text extracted from one document (or the transcript of an audio file), in pages: offset and max_chars select the part, and the reply says how long the whole text is.

tools.name: list_knowledge_notes
tools.description: The notes written in a notebook, with their full text.

tools.name: list_knowledge_chats
tools.description: The conversations held with a notebook, newest first.

tools.name: get_knowledge_chat
tools.description: One conversation with a notebook: the questions and the answers with their sources.

tools.name: get_knowledge_answer
tools.description: The state and, once ready, the answer of a question asked with ask_knowledge_notebook.

tools.name: get_knowledge_notebook_access
tools.description: Who can use a notebook: the apps that answer from it and the owner's agents it is connected to.

tools.name: get_app_knowledge_access
tools.description: Which of the owner's notebooks an app's AI may answer from, and the ones it could be given.

tools.name: list_knowledge_webhooks
tools.description: The ingest webhooks that let an external system add files to a notebook, with their state. Their URLs are secrets and are shown only on the Brain screen, where webhooks are created.

tools.name: get_knowledge_redaction_run
tools.description: A sensitive-data scan: per document its state and what was found (category, the text, the suggested replacement, confidence), and what was applied.

tools.name: get_knowledge_redaction_policy
tools.description: A notebook's automatic redaction policy for new uploads.

tools.name: get_knowledge_redaction_log
tools.description: What was redacted in one document, by category and count, and whether the original was kept.

tools.name: get_knowledge_access_log
tools.description: Who opened, asked or changed the notebooks, newest first: people, apps and agents.

tools.name: list_failed_knowledge_documents
tools.description: Documents whose processing failed, with the error, so they can be retried or replaced.

tools.name: create_knowledge_notebook
tools.description: Create an empty notebook, optionally inside a folder.

tools.name: rename_knowledge_notebook
tools.description: Change a notebook's title; its documents and notes stay as they are.

tools.name: create_knowledge_folder
tools.description: Create a folder for notebooks, optionally inside another folder.

tools.name: update_knowledge_folder
tools.description: Rename a folder, or move it: parent_id is the new parent, an empty string moves it to the top.

tools.name: move_knowledge_notebook
tools.description: File a notebook in a folder; an empty or missing folder_id moves it to the top.

tools.name: set_app_knowledge_access
tools.description: Choose which of the owner's notebooks an app's AI may answer from. The list replaces the current one; an empty list gives it none.

tools.name: add_knowledge_note
tools.description: Write a note into a notebook; agents and apps answer from it like from a document.

tools.name: update_knowledge_note
tools.description: Replace the text of a note in a notebook with new text.

tools.name: add_knowledge_document
tools.description: Add a document to a notebook: plain text, or a file (PDF, Word, a spreadsheet, an image or audio) as base64. It is processed in the background (audio is transcribed); list_knowledge_documents shows when it is ready. The same file twice is recognised.

tools.name: import_knowledge_audio_url
tools.description: Download a public audio file (a recording, a podcast episode) into a new notebook and transcribe it there.

tools.name: rename_knowledge_document
tools.description: Set the name a document is shown under (its file name stays); an empty name clears it.

tools.name: retry_knowledge_document
tools.description: Process a document again after it failed or stalled.

tools.name: ask_knowledge_notebook
tools.description: Ask a notebook a question; the answer comes from its documents, with sources. Waits up to 25 seconds for the answer, otherwise returns the query_job_id for get_knowledge_answer. Without chat_session_id a new conversation starts.

tools.name: set_knowledge_webhook_enabled
tools.description: Turn an ingest webhook off (posts are refused) or on again.

tools.name: scan_knowledge_for_sensitive_data
tools.description: Scan documents for personal or sensitive information, or for what the owner's instructions describe. Only finds; nothing changes until apply_knowledge_redaction. Runs in the background; read it with get_knowledge_redaction_run.

tools.name: apply_knowledge_redaction
tools.description: Redact the chosen findings of a scan: approved maps each document id to the finding ids to replace. The original text is kept, so revert_knowledge_redaction can undo it.

tools.name: revert_knowledge_redaction
tools.description: Undo an applied redaction: the documents get their original text back.

tools.name: set_knowledge_redaction_policy
tools.description: Set a notebook's automatic redaction for new uploads: on or off, what to find (instructions), whether findings above min_confidence are applied at once. Originals are always kept.

tools.name: list_whatsapp_triggers
tools.description: The app's WhatsApp triggers: the message sent to a customer when a record is created, the page and entity, the phone field, the sending number and whether it is on.

tools.name: get_whatsapp_trigger_options
tools.description: What a WhatsApp trigger can use in this app: the owner's WhatsApp numbers and flows, and the pages, entities and fields that create records.

tools.name: list_whatsapp_trigger_logs
tools.description: What the app's WhatsApp triggers sent, newest first, with the outcome of each send.

tools.name: create_whatsapp_trigger
tools.description: Save a WhatsApp trigger for record-created events. It is saved switched off and messages no one. Switching it on is done by the owner on the app's Automations screen in Fine Structure.

tools.name: update_whatsapp_trigger
tools.description: Change a trigger that is switched off: page, entity, fields, message, number or flow. Only the fields given change. A trigger that is on is turned off first with disable_whatsapp_trigger.

tools.name: disable_whatsapp_trigger
tools.description: Switch a WhatsApp trigger off: new records no longer send its message. It stays saved.

tools.name: send_whatsapp_trigger_test
tools.description: Send a saved trigger's message once to the owner's own verified WhatsApp number, rendered with a sample record, from the trigger's sending number. It never goes to anyone else.

tools.name: suggest_whatsapp_trigger_message
tools.description: Have the AI write a WhatsApp message for a trigger from the page it follows, the app's brain and the record fields. Returns text to review; nothing is saved or sent.

detail: Tool "remove_app_member" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "Remove a generated-app runtime member." → after: "Remove a person's access to the app. They are blocked, as with block_app_member: their sessions end and the address can neither sign in nor sign up again. Nothing is deleted, and unblock_app_member gives the access back."

remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
